value.hook: Open before appending anything to a message a seat receives (a line, a note, a refreshed notice), reading or re-checking held FYIs, or writing a validate-first preflight
value.title: Adding text to a turn at delivery: hand-over points, never stored (F169, F170, 226 r2)

sections.name: body
sections.value:
What #214 (F169/F170) and #212 round 2 taught, from spoonbill's blocks:

1. Text computed at admission goes stale for queued turns. A queued row's payload is what gets delivered later. Compute per-recipient text at hand-over and never store it. The hand-over points are:
   - `DeliveryService::claim_inbox_inner` (extension, native and pull claims);
   - `DrainWorker::handle_claim` (pane typing);
   - the Socket and TypedBody rungs in `arrive`, which deliver directly.
   The hook in #214 is `fyi_notes::noted` behind an optional `with_notes` port, so tests that build `DeliveryService::new` are untouched.
2. Plan 184's leftover recognition needs identical text across retries: `own_leftover` compares against the same text. If you append something that changes over time (ages, counts), keep it per job for retries (the worker's `noted` cache), and queue a deferred direct attempt with the text it staged.
3. FYIs are attached inside a synchronous closure in the store transaction (`AttachFyis`). Take any async snapshot first (registry, sizes), then capture it in the closure. Every place that shows FYIs needs the same treatment: ride-along, warm flush, hook claim, `fyi-read` (a digest's full read) and `--pending`. Spoonbill found the one I missed.
4. `SeatDescriptor.role` is empty on a bare registry read; `join_roles` fills it. Is this a PA? means reading `seat_roles` (`SqliteOrchestration::seat_role`).
5. Pending FYIs are in the `fyis` table (pending-only partial index). The Queue port only counts or claims one seat's pile, so fleet-wide reads go through `SqliteOrchestration` (`pending_peer_fyi_backlogs`, `pending_fyis`).
6. Watchdog tests run rounds on simulated time, but FYI `held_at` comes from the real delivery clock. Compare times from one clock: the `fyi-stall` claim records `newest_ms` rather than using `claimed_at`.
7. Any size cap must cover the delivered body, including what a later layer appends (the PA line). Budget for the worst case: 64-byte seat ids.
8. Validate-first (226 r2): a preflight must run the send path's own pure rules, not just the parser. Pull each rule out as a pure function both sides call (`role_send::check`, `cold_wake::forced_reason`), and prove nothing ran with a positive control.
9. Changing a golden fixture means re-recording its sha256, bytes and `answer` in `crates/testkit/fixtures/MANIFEST.toml`. When CI is the Rust proof, confirm the new tests ran in its junit-linux artifact.
